phase: Phase 9.3 — cross-document content-addressed store: three accounting universes vs per-file LZ and generic content-defined-chunk dedup
cohort: evidence/corpus/phase9 — 37 locally generated files, 5,579,469 B source, 10 strata (p7, repeat-bin, repeat-pdf, shared-payload, shared-bin, dup-resource, reexport, one-changed, incremental, shifted). No third-party bytes; generator tools/store-cohort.sh; ledger cohort.json.
claim: On this cohort the EmbeddedStore's unique-reachable universe (U = 3,369,900 B) LOSES the store axis: it is larger than per-file min LZ (1,304,307 B) and larger than the strongest pinned content-defined-chunk dedup (borg 1.2.4, chunker 10,15,11,127, compression none: 771,383 B; the same with zstd,19 chunk compression: 210,836 B). Object-granularity sharing beats both baselines on exactly one stratum — repeat-bin, byte-identical opaque binaries (U = 133,048 B vs per-file LZ 524,308 B, CDC raw 140,640 B, CDC+zstd 133,865 B). On shared-payload (the expected win fixture), shared-bin, one-changed, incremental, reexport and shifted the store loses to CDC; on repeat-pdf it does no dedup at all. Cause: the auto-winning candidate for most PDFs keeps the document's bulk in entropy channels and program INLINE ops, which `externalize` does not externalise, so only whole DRA objects (usually the entire file for RAW winners) are shared.
verification: Every one of the 37 standalone descriptors and every one of the 37 store-backed roots was decoded and `cmp`-ed byte-exact; `store account` closure reported dangling = 0. `verify` has no resolver and so was run on the standalone form only; the store-backed form is gated by decode --store (which re-checks the whole-source INTEGRITY SHA-256) + cmp.
